tagline: The Worlds anthem whose hook came true for DRX.
headline: Lil Nas X's divisive Worlds 2022 anthem became a Hot 100 hit, then the soundtrack to DRX's Cinderella run.
summary: Released on September 22, 2022 as the anthem of the League of Legends World Championship, "STAR WALKIN'" was the centrepiece of Riot's tongue-in-cheek campaign naming Lil Nas X the "President of League of Legends." Many fans first complained that it didn't feel like a Worlds anthem and joked it sounded better at 1.25x speed, but it debuted at No. 32 on the Billboard Hot 100 and later went Platinum in the US. Then DRX, the LCK's last seed, climbed out of the Play-In stage and beat T1 at Chase Center on the night Lil Nas X performed it there, and the hook "Don't ever say it's over if I'm breathing" started to sound like a prophecy.

story.heading: Mr. President
story.body:
On September 15, 2022, Riot introduced a new executive: Lil Nas X, "President of League of Legends." He was already a two-time Grammy winner with three Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s. In a mockumentary-style promo, he takes over Riot's offices, asks for a nude Udyr skin he calls "Nudyr," and plays the new anthem on office appliances, including a fridge and a photocopier. Meanwhile, League's official Twitter account was renamed "LoLNasX." He promised to be "the greatest President, of League of Legends, of all time," and Riot's global head of League esports, Naz Aletaha, called him "the most electrifying name in music."

The joke came with real duties. The President would release the Worlds 2022 anthem, co-design a champion skin and perform live at the World Final in San Francisco on November 5. Carrie Dunn, Riot's global head of esports creative, said the studio wanted the anthem to have a North American flair while embodying the year's "One & Only" Worlds brand.

story.heading: Fifty hooks
story.body:
Lil Nas X admitted in an Apple Music interview that he was "not really much of a gamer anymore." The hard part was the chorus: he said he went through "30 different, 40 different, 50" hooks before landing on the one that stuck. He wrote the song with Atia "Ink" Boggs, Omer Fedi and Cirkut (Henry Walter) and produced it with Cirkut and Fedi, and Serban Ghenea mixed it.

The result splits the difference between pop and rap: a chant-like pop hook alternates with rapped verses about proving doubters wrong. The hook boils that down to one line: "Don't ever say it's over if I'm breathing." According to Songfacts, he first performed the song as an encore on September 6, 2022, the opening night of his Long Live Montero tour in Detroit, more than two weeks before its release.

story.heading: San Francisco, mech'd up
story.body:
The single and its music video arrived on September 22, 2022, released through Columbia Records and Riot Games. The animated video was made with the animation studio The Line and directed by Wesley Louis. It tours San Francisco, the city hosting the final, with four pros, one from each major region: Gen.G's Chovy (LCK), Team Liquid's CoreJJ (LCS), EDward Gaming's Meiko (LPL) and Fnatic's Humanoid (LEC). They pose on the Golden Gate Bridge for the title card, and later the city tears loose around them as giant mech versions of Azir, Rell, Thresh and Twisted Fate rise over it.

Riot said almost every shot hides an Easter egg, from regional-league flair to fun facts about the pros. The third chorus works like a trading-card roll call that pairs each player with his mech, and YouTube's replay data shows it is the part viewers rewatch most. The last chorus brings in an animated Lil Nas X in a red puffer jacket, standing with the four pros in front of their giant machines.

story.heading: Try it at 1.25x
story.body:
League fans were not convinced at first. Sportskeeda reported a wave of negative feedback from players, pros and casters: some felt the video looked more like a promo for the new mech skins than a Worlds film, others that it lacked passion and direction. Upcomer noted that comments quickly pointed at CoreJJ, whose Team Liquid had not even qualified, and summed up the main complaint: it felt like a good Lil Nas X song rather than a Worlds anthem.

Then came the meme. LS tweeted that the song sounded better at 1.25x speed, and fans escalated to 2x so it would be over sooner. Lil Nas X joined in on TikTok and Twitter with a sarcastic listening guide that opened with the same 1.25x advice. Music critics were kinder. Billboard's Jason Lipshutz called it "far from a corporate stopgap," said it "works even without the gamer context," and predicted another hit for an artist who was already piling them up.

story.heading: A hit beyond the Rift
story.body:
Billboard was right. "STAR WALKIN'" entered the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 32 on the chart dated October 8, 2022. It reached No. 21 on the Billboard Global 200 and No. 10 on Billboard's Pop Airplay chart. Elsewhere it peaked at No. 8 on the Dutch Top 40, No. 11 in Germany and No. 17 on the Canadian Hot 100.

It kept going long after the Summoner's Cup was lifted. The song showed up on 2023 year-end charts, including No. 61 on Canada's Hot 100 and No. 41 on US Mainstream Top 40 radio. The RIAA certified it Platinum on April 5, 2024, and France certified it Diamond. For a song written to promote an esports tournament, it had an unusually long life on pop radio.

story.heading: One night at Chase Center
story.body:
The President stayed busy all autumn. On October 17 Riot posted a video of him introducing a K'Sante skin. Prestige Empyrean K'Sante, co-designed with him, reached the test server alongside the new champion on October 18 and launched on November 3, earnable with Worlds tokens until November 14. On November 2, Riot released his "final presidential address," which set up his live performance.

The World Final took place on November 5, 2022 at Chase Center in San Francisco. Carrie Dunn called the build Riot's most ambitious stage build ever: about 470,000 pounds of gear were lifted into the air and the venue crew worked around the clock for 96 hours. The show was built in three acts around three songs. It opened with 2WEI's *The Call*, performed by Edda Hayes and Louis Leibfried, Jackson Wang performed *Fire to the Fuse*, and Lil Nas X headlined with *STAR WALKIN'* before DRX and T1 took the stage.

story.heading: Don't ever say it's over
story.body:
DRX were long shots. As South Korea's last seed, they started in the Play-In stage in Mexico City and went through the groups in New York. They then knocked out defending champions EDward Gaming and the LCK's top seed Gen.G, and beat three-time champions T1 3–2 in San Francisco. They were the first Play-In team ever to win Worlds. Kingen was named Finals MVP, and Deft, who had debuted as a teenager in 2013, finally won the title he had chased for nearly a decade. According to Esports Charts, the final peaked at about 5.1 million viewers.

The anthem's hook suddenly sounded like a prophecy. GosuGamers wrote that DRX's run, by a team that could barely qualify, put the song's opening line in a different light.

In Korea the same idea had already become a catchphrase. After a group-stage loss in October, Deft had told reporters the team could still win as long as it did not fall apart from within, and a highlight-video thumbnail turned that into "What matters is an unbroken heart." By December the phrase was on a Korean flag at the World Cup, where defender Kwon Kyung-won wrapped himself in it after the win over Portugal. The hook and Deft's motto carried the same message.

story.heading: From punchline to prophecy
story.body:
Its reputation turned around fast. A song first mocked as the anthem that needed to be sped up is now tied to one of League's great underdog stories, sung on the night a Play-In team beat T1 for the title.

It also kept its place in the series' official history. When iam8bit pressed ten years of Worlds anthems onto vinyl in *League of Legends Worlds Anthems Vol. 1: 2014–2023*, "STAR WALKIN'" was the 2022 entry, between PVRIS' *Burn It All Down* and NewJeans' *GODS*. The music video has now passed 112 million views and 1.2 million likes, and the Chase Center performance has over 12 million views of its own.

whyItMatters: It was the centrepiece of Riot's "President of League of Legends" campaign: a Worlds anthem, a co-designed Prestige K'Sante skin and a live performance at the World Final, all from one pop star.
It crossed over: it debuted at No. 32 on the Billboard Hot 100, reached No. 10 on Pop Airplay, and went Platinum in the US and Diamond in France.
Its rocky launch is part of the story. Fans said it didn't feel like a Worlds anthem, and the 1.25x-speed jokes became a meme Lil Nas X himself joined.
It soundtracked DRX's Cinderella run: Lil Nas X performed it at Chase Center before the first Play-In team ever won Worlds and Deft won his first title.
Its hook, "Don't ever say it's over if I'm breathing," echoed Deft's "unbroken heart" motto, which became a national catchphrase in Korea that winter.
It is the 2022 entry on the Worlds Anthems Vol. 1 (2014–2023) vinyl from iam8bit.

communityMoments.title: The President takes office
communityMoments.description: Riot named Lil Nas X "President of League of Legends" in a mockumentary promo. He asked for a "Nudyr" skin and played the anthem on office appliances, and League's Twitter account was renamed "LoLNasX."

communityMoments.title: The anthem and video drop
communityMoments.description: LoL Esports premiered the single and The Line's animated video starring Chovy, CoreJJ, Meiko and Humanoid, with giant mech champions rising over San Francisco.

communityMoments.title: "Was it rushed?"
communityMoments.description: Sportskeeda collected a wave of negative reactions: a video that looked like a mech-skin ad and a song that felt more like Lil Nas X than Worlds. Others noted that CoreJJ's Team Liquid had not qualified.

communityMoments.title: Try it at 1.25x speed

communityMoments.title: The final presidential address
communityMoments.description: Three days before the final, Riot posted Lil Nas X's mock-presidential address, which set up his live Worlds performance.

communityMoments.title: Live at Chase Center
communityMoments.description: Lil Nas X headlined the Worlds 2022 Finals Opening Ceremony in San Francisco, a three-act show that also featured Jackson Wang, Edda Hayes and Louis Leibfried.

communityMoments.title: DRX make the hook come true
communityMoments.description: DRX beat T1 3–2 to become the first Play-In team to win Worlds. GosuGamers noted that their run put the anthem's opening line in a different light.

communityMoments.description: Deft's "What matters is an unbroken heart" motto from DRX's run reached South Korea's World Cup squad: after beating Portugal, Kwon Kyung-won wrapped himself in a flag bearing the phrase.

keyMoments.label: The Golden Gate above the fog
keyMoments.description: The video opens on the Golden Gate Bridge rising out of the fog over San Francisco, the host city of the final.

keyMoments.label: The hook and the title card
keyMoments.description: Chovy, CoreJJ, Meiko and Humanoid pose on the Golden Gate Bridge as "Don't ever say it's over if I'm breathing" plays, and the STAR WALKIN' title slams across the frame.

keyMoments.label: Fans of every region
keyMoments.description: EDG supporters with "Crazy is our game" banners pack the streets, and fans gather beneath a giant LIL NAS X billboard.

keyMoments.label: The city lifts off
keyMoments.description: During the second chorus a pro spreads his arms, and paving stones, piers and buildings tear loose and float into the sky.

keyMoments.label: Mechs over San Francisco
keyMoments.description: A giant golden mech towers over a crowd on a city hill, then a mech Twisted Fate strides past the Golden Gate Bridge through the haze.

keyMoments.label: Trading-card roll call
keyMoments.description: The third chorus flashes graphic title cards for each pro and his mech champion: Meiko with Thresh, Chovy with Azir, then CoreJJ and Humanoid. YouTube marks this as the video's most-replayed stretch.

keyMoments.label: Lil Nas X joins the squad
keyMoments.description: In the final chorus, an animated Lil Nas X in a red puffer jacket stands with the four pros in front of their mechs as the Worlds 2022 dates (9/29 – 11/5) appear.

keyMoments.label: Worlds 22
keyMoments.description: The video closes on the Worlds 22 logo over rippling white jersey fabric.

featuredClip.description: The hook plays on the Golden Gate Bridge: four pros pose as the giant red STAR WALKIN' title and "lil nas x" slam into the frame.
